why:
phase-482 W4 (2026-10-07): PUBLIC on `rclcpp_lifecycle::LifecycleNode`, taking a `nros::ManagedEntityInterface*` whose own move and destructor keep the node's intrusive list correct. Publishers made by `create_publisher` are added already, so a ported node rarely calls it.

Before phase-482 W4: upstream's is PROTECTED (rclcpp_lifecycle/lifecycle_node.hpp:976 in humble, taking a `std::weak_ptr<ManagedEntityInterface>`) because its own `create_publisher` calls it for you; a user never names it. Ours is PUBLIC because our `LifecycleNode` is a mixin over the executor's state machine and creates no entities -- `rclcpp::Node` does (see `LifecycleNode::bind`) -- so registration is the caller's line. The registry is an INTRUSIVE list rather than upstream's `std::vector<std::weak_ptr<...>>`: there is no allocator and no `shared_ptr` on a freestanding target, and a fixed array would put a capacity into the class layout, which `check-cpp-capability-layout` forbids. Cost of that shape, stated: an entity must outlive the node and must not be added to two nodes; adding one twice is REFUSED (`AlreadyExists`) rather than corrupting the list.
